program: RiCON: Train for The Great Cordillera
source: Edify Endurance, TGC 24-Week Training Schedule (100K verbatim; 60K derived)
note_60k: No 60K plan existed in the source file. This 60K is derived from the 100K, with identical periodization and session types but reduced volume and vertical for ~60km / 4,200m gain. Requires Edify Endurance sign-off before publishing.

rpe_scale.label: Easy / Recovery
rpe_scale.purpose: Aerobic base, recovery, long endurance fat oxidation

rpe_scale.label: Moderate / Steady
rpe_scale.purpose: Steady mountain-hike simulation, sustained hill intervals

rpe_scale.label: Hard / Very Hard
rpe_scale.purpose: VO2 max, steep short hill repeats (used sparingly)

uesca_principles.name: Muscular Endurance
uesca_principles.desc: Training muscles to withstand prolonged vertical stress.
uesca_principles.implementation: High-volume stair climbing, incline treadmill power-walking, heavy lower-body strength.

uesca_principles.name: Biomechanical Specificity
uesca_principles.desc: Replicating the movement patterns of mountain trails.
uesca_principles.implementation: Eccentric quadriceps loading (lunges, step-downs) for relentless descents.

uesca_principles.name: Metabolic Efficiency
uesca_principles.desc: Optimizing fat oxidation for multi-hour events.
uesca_principles.implementation: Keep all easy runs and long back-to-backs strictly Zone 2 / low intensity.

uesca_principles.name: Gear & Nutrition Simulation
uesca_principles.desc: Testing race-day gear and multi-hour gut fueling.
uesca_principles.implementation: Wear the full race vest with hydration/food on Saturday & Sunday efforts.

strength_routine.name: Mountain Resilience Strength Routine
strength_routine.cadence: 2x/week during build phases (Tue or Thu, after the easy run). Minimal gym equipment.
strength_routine.rationale: To survive 4,200m–7,000m of vertical stress, general strength is not enough. Athletes without mountain access must train eccentric loading: strengthening muscles while they lengthen, to prepare quads for hours of downhill braking.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raises
exercises.purpose: Achilles & calf elasticity for steep climbing.

exercises.name: Tibialis Raises
exercises.purpose: Shin resilience to prevent splints during power-hiking.

exercises.name: Eccentric-Focused Goblet Squat
exercises.purpose: Simulates downhill braking to bulletproof the quads.

exercises.name: Deficit Reverse Lunges
exercises.purpose: Glutes & hamstrings for climbing power on high gradients.

exercises.name: Weighted Step-Downs
exercises.purpose: Single-leg eccentric stability. Most vital for flat-landers.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlifts
exercises.purpose: Fixes imbalances, guards hamstrings against late-race cramping.

exercises.name: Altitude Drops (Box Snap-Downs)
exercises.focus: Drop from 12-24" box, land soft, hold 2s
exercises.purpose: Trains the nervous system to absorb impact and protect knees.

exercises.name: Continuous Box Jumps
exercises.purpose: Fast-twitch recruitment for clearing obstacles under fatigue.

coach_brief: Week 1, Base 1. You're building the aerobic floor. Easy volume, light hills, time on feet. Nothing heroic yet.
Your anchor this week is Saturday's 2h Hilly Run with 300m of vert.
Total volume: 7 hours. Keep your easy days genuinely easy at RPE 2-3. The hard work is in the hills and the long run.
Week 2, Base 1. You're building the aerobic floor. Easy volume, light hills, time on feet. Nothing heroic yet.
Your anchor this week is Saturday's 2.5h Hilly Run with 400m of vert.
Total volume: 7.5 hours. Keep your easy days genuinely easy at RPE 2-3. The hard work is in the hills and the long run.
Week 3, Base 1. You're building the aerobic floor. Easy volume, light hills, time on feet. Nothing heroic yet.
Your anchor this week is Saturday's 2.5h Hilly Run with 500m of vert.
Total volume: 8 hours. Keep your easy days genuinely easy at RPE 2-3. The hard work is in the hills and the long run.
Week 4, Base 1. You're building the aerobic floor. Easy volume, light hills, time on feet. Nothing heroic yet.
Your anchor this week is Saturday's 3h Hilly Run with 600m of vert.
Total volume: 8.5 hours. Keep your easy days genuinely easy at RPE 2-3. The hard work is in the hills and the long run.
Week 5, Deload 1. Pull back this week. The work sticks when you recover.
Saturday is 1.5h Flat Trail/Park Run. That's enough.
Volume drops to 5.5 hours this week. Let the last block settle.
Wednesday is a short mobility session, not a hard workout. That's intentional. Thursday and Friday are longer easy days that build volume without burning intensity before Saturday.
Saturday's 3-hour hilly run at RPE 4-5 is the anchor session. Keep Friday's core work genuinely complementary; it should not leave you sore going into the long run.
Sunday is an easy road or trail run. Keep it at RPE 3-4 and treat it as flushing out Saturday's effort, not adding to it.

Use the weekend long runs to practice wearing your race vest, taking in energy gels or other race nutrition, hydration timing (700ml to 1000ml per hour), and solid food. What works in training is what you trust in November.

days.title: Mobility Session (e.g. Yoga, Mini Band Workout)
days.raw: 0.5h Mobility Session (e.g. Yoga, Mini Band Workout)

weeks.block_goal: 800m x 2 (RPE 7-8) rest 2 mins + 400m x 4-6 reps (RPE 8-9), 90s to 120s recovery, standing
coach_brief: Monday is optional. Take the mobility session if your body is responding well, take full rest if you need it. There is no wrong answer.

Tuesday adds core work after the easy run. Wednesday's hill repeats are the main quality session: 30 minutes easy, then 10 to 12 short hard reps with walk-back recovery, then 30 minutes easy to close.
Thursday introduces tempo for the first time this phase. The structure is easy warm-up, 30 minutes at RPE 6, then a full cooldown. Keep the tempo honest, not harder than prescribed.

days.title: Mobility Session  or REST (e.g. Yoga, Mini Band Workout)
days.raw: 0.5h Mobility Session (e.g. Yoga, Mini Band Workout) or REST

days.title: Short Steep Hill Repeats
days.detail: 30 min easy + 1 min x 10-12 reps + 30 min easy
days.raw: 1.5h Short Steep Hill Repeats (30 min easy + 1 min x 10-12 reps + 30 min easy)

weeks.block_goal: 2 mins x 10 at RPE 9 (20 mins speed work), 2 mins rest, 1:1 ratio
coach_brief: For the next 2 to 3 weeks, our training plan includes one of the most important sessions for preparing your legs for The Great Cordillera 100. This workout builds the strength, endurance, and pacing you will need for the long climbs and technical terrain on race day.
Sunday's power-walk keeps the legs moving without adding more damage, so don't skip it and don't make it harder than it needs to be.

featured_workout.title: Pyramidal Hill Overloads
featured_workout.intro: A pyramid of timed uphill efforts with equal recovery. The structure trains you to surge when terrain demands it, back off on descent, and repeat — which is exactly how mountain racing moves. Use this guide for all three weeks.

sections.heading: Main Set
items: 5 mins uphill @ RPE 8 (controlled, not all out)

sections.heading: Recovery
items: Easy jog or walk downhill for approximately the same duration as each work interval.

sections.heading: Cooldown
items: Easy running until you reach 1.5 hours total training time.

sections.heading: Coaching Tips
items: Maintain a quick cadence. Don't sprint the shorter intervals.
Keep your posture tall with a slight lean from the ankles.
If the climb becomes too steep, switch to a strong power hike. This is exactly what you'll do during many sections of TGC 100.
Finish the workout feeling like you could complete one more interval. Leave a little in the tank.

sections.heading: Why This Workout?
items: Fatigue resistance for long mountain ultras like The Great Cordillera 100

sections.heading: No Hills? No Problem!
sections.note: Not everyone has access to long climbs, and that's perfectly okay. Here are some alternatives that provide a similar training stimulus.
items: Option 1 – Flat Tempo Pyramid (Recommended): complete the same 1-2-3-4-5-4-3-2-1 structure on flat terrain at RPE 6-8, easy jog recovery for the same duration as each interval, focus on consistent effort instead of pace.
Option 2 – Treadmill: set incline to 5-8%, complete the same pyramid at RPE 6-8, avoid holding handrails.
Option 3 – Stairs or Parking Garage: run or power hike continuously during each interval, walk back down for recovery, excellent for building climbing-specific strength.

sections.heading: Remember
items: Keep your cadence smooth and consistent.

coach_brief: Base 2 started with a 3-hour Saturday and 700m of gain. This week it's 4.5 hours and 1000m, and if that progression doesn't feel like a massive jump from where you started, you've been doing the work.

Wednesday's pyramidal session is about surging and recovering repeatedly, which is how mountain terrain actually moves. It's also worth starting to think through race execution in real terms this week, when you eat and how you handle the big climbs, because November is closer than it looks.

days.raw: 2h Flat trail or soft surfaces jog (RPE 2)

coach_brief: Base 2 was about load. Build 1 is about specificity, and Wednesday's stairway loops are where that starts. Find stairs anywhere and put in ninety minutes of vertical time at sustained effort.
Saturday matches the Base 2 peak in hours and gain, but you're arriving with fresher legs, and that usually shows up in the back half of the run.

items: Option 1 – Flat Tempo Pyramid (Recommended): complete the same 1-2-3-4-5-4-3-2-1 structure on flat terrain at RPE 6-8, easy jog recovery for the same duration as each interval, focus on consistent effort instead of pace.
Option 2 – Treadmill: set incline to 5-8%, complete the same pyramid at RPE 6-8, avoid holding handrails.
Option 3 – Stairs or Parking Garage: run or power hike continuously during each interval, walk back down for recovery, excellent for building climbing-specific strength.

sections.heading: Remember
items: Keep your cadence smooth and consistent.

days.raw: 1.75h Flat trail or soft surfaces jog (RPE 2)

coach_brief: Base 2 was about load. Build 1 is about specificity, and Wednesday's stairway loops are where that starts. Find stairs anywhere and put in ninety minutes of vertical time at sustained effort.
Saturday matches the Base 2 peak in hours and gain, but you're arriving with fresher legs, and that usually shows up in the back half of the run.
Week 12, Build 1. Now you sharpen the climb and the descent. Stairway loops, urban vert, downhill control.
Your anchor this week is Saturday's 5h High Vert Focus with 1200m of vert.
Total volume: 11.5 hours. Keep your easy days genuinely easy at RPE 2-3. The hard work is in the hills and the long run.

Rest, shake out, handle logistics. Get to the start line fresh.
